title: You only use 10% of your brain?

segments.text: You only use {10%|ten percent} of your brain. Well, that's not exactly true. You use pretty much all of it.
Brain scans show activity all over. Different parts light up for seeing, moving, talking and remembering, and over a single day, almost every part gets a turn.
Here's the wild part. Your brain is only about {2%|two percent} of your body weight, but it burns around {20%|twenty percent} of your energy. If most of it did nothing, that would be a terrible deal.
Even when you sleep, it doesn't switch off. It sorts your memories and cleans itself up.
That's not all. Your brain has no pain receptors of its own, which is why some people stay awake during brain surgery.
In fact, signals can race along your nerves at over {250 mph.|two hundred fifty miles per hour.}
So no, you don't use {10%|ten percent} of your brain. You're using all of it, right now.
